title: Integral split radical quotient and simply connected cover
statement:
Let $H$ be a split reductive $\mathbf Z$-group scheme with a split maximal torus and a Borel subgroup scheme containing it. A reductive group scheme over a commutative ring is a smooth affine finitely presented group scheme with connected geometric fibres having no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; unipotent means that in a faithful matrix representation each geometric point $u$ satisfies $(u-I)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. Group objects use the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over the specified spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with smooth, affine, finite presentation and connected as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A split maximal torus is a subgroup scheme isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ with fibrewise maximal tori, where $\mathbf G_m(B)=B^\times$ and $r\geq0$. A Borel subgroup scheme has geometric fibres maximal smooth connected solvable subgroups; solvable means that iterated commutator subgroups eventually become trivial. There are a closed [def-weil-closed-immersion] central subgroup scheme $T\simeq\mathbf G_{m,\mathbf Z}^r$ for some $r\geq0$, a split semisimple $\mathbf Z$-group scheme $Q$, a split semisimple simply connected $\mathbf Z$-group scheme $S$, and exact sequences of group schemes
$$1\longrightarrow T\longrightarrow H\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow1,
\qquad 1\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow S\xrightarrow{\pi}Q\longrightarrow1.$$
Here $F$ is central and finite locally free over $\mathbf Z$ (its coordinate algebra is a finitely generated projective $\mathbf Z$-module). Exact means that the first arrow identifies the scheme-theoretic kernel, and the last arrow is faithfully flat (flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and surjective) and locally of finite presentation and represents the fppf sheaf quotient; fppf covers are jointly surjective flat locally finitely presented families. Semisimple means smooth affine finitely presented with connected geometric fibres having no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup. Simply connected means that every central isogeny onto a geometric fibre from a connected semisimple group is an isomorphism; a central isogeny is a surjective homomorphism with finite central scheme-theoretic kernel. Both sequences remain exact after every ring base change $\mathbf Z\to B$, with the displayed split, semisimple and simply connected properties retained. Trivial tori and trivial semisimple groups are allowed.

source.place: Example 5.1.7, printed pp.138-139 (root-lattice centre); Theorem 5.3.1 and Corollary 5.3.3, pp.160-164 (maximal central torus and semisimple quotient); Theorem 6.1.16, p.196, and Exercise 6.5.2(i), p.235 (split simply connected covering). Use the split root datum over Z; finite central kernels are scheme-theoretic. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
Write $U=D_{\mathbf Z}(M)$ for the given split maximal torus of $H$. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-split-root-datum] to obtain the constant roots $\Phi$ and coroots, valid on every geometric fibre. Put $L=\mathbf Z\Phi$. The relative centre formula [lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel] gives the scheme-theoretic closed centre
$$Z(H)=D_{\mathbf Z}(M/L)\subseteq U.$$
The latter lemma applies over $\mathbf Z$, a nonzero Noetherian ring, and its constant-support hypothesis is exactly supplied by the first citation. In particular this is an identity of group schemes, not merely of points over fields.

Set $A=M/L$, let $A_{\mathrm{tor}}$ be its subgroup of finite-order elements, and put $C=A/A_{\mathrm{tor}}$. The finitely generated abelian-group structure theorem makes $A_{\mathrm{tor}}$ finite and $C\simeq\mathbf Z^r$ for some $r\geq0$. The surjection $M\twoheadrightarrow A\twoheadrightarrow C$ induces a closed immersion $T=D_{\mathbf Z}(C)\hookrightarrow Z(H)$ by relative diagonalizable duality. Thus $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ is central and closed in $H$ (in coordinates the two successive quotient maps are surjective). For any algebraically closed field $k$, a subtorus of $Z(H)_k=D_k(A)$ has character group free of finite rank. Its character map from $A$ kills $A_{\mathrm{tor}}$, so its inclusion factors through $D_k(C)=T_k$. Hence $T_k$ is the largest central subtorus. This elementary factorization uses the duality statement over $k$ and does not replace the centre by its reduction.

source.place: Example 5.1.7, pp.138-139; Remark B.1.2, pp.280-281 (largest torus in a diagonalizable group).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-central-multiplicative-quotient] over $\mathbf Z$ to the closed central multiplicative-type subgroup $T\subseteq H$. It represents $Q=H/T$ by a reductive integral group, with kernel $T$, and makes $p:H\to Q$ faithfully flat and finitely presented and a represented fppf quotient. Formation of this quotient and the maximal torus $U/T$ commute with arbitrary base change. Put $N=\ker(M\to C)$. The relative diagonalizable quotient formula identifies $U/T=D_{\mathbf Z}(N)$; $N$ is free of finite rank by [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free]. Therefore $Q$ has a split maximal torus. For every algebraically closed $k$, step 2 identifies $T_k$ with the largest central torus of $H_k$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-radical-quotient] this is its radical and $H_k/T_k$ is semisimple. The arbitrary-base-change clause of the relative quotient identifies this quotient with $Q_k$. Thus $Q$ is split semisimple.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.5, pp.100-101; Example 5.1.7 and Corollary 5.3.3, pp.138-139,164. Field radical criterion: Milne Corollary 17.62(b)-(d), pp.372-373.

proof.text:
Extract the root datum $(X,\Psi,X^\vee,\Psi^\vee)$ of the split semisimple group $Q$ by [lem-sfb-integral-split-root-datum]. Its roots span $V=X\otimes\mathbf Q$. Apply [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding] with this datum. Since the root span is all of $V$, its complementary central space is zero. Its weight lattice
$$P=\{v\in V:\langle v,\beta^\vee\rangle\in\mathbf Z\text{ for every }\beta\in\Psi\}$$
is free of finite rank, and $X\subseteq P$ with finite index: the lemma's map $j$ is precisely this inclusion because its root-space projection is the identity. Every root is in $X$, so the inclusion fixes all roots and the coroot restrictions agree.

source.place: Example 5.1.7, pp.138-139; Theorem 6.1.16 and Exercise 6.5.2(i), pp.196,235. Weight-lattice construction: Milne Appendix C and Section 23h.

proof.text: Use the roots $\Psi\subset P$ and coroot functionals on $P$ induced by the rational coroots. They form a reduced root datum: the pairing is integral by the definition of $P$; $s_\beta(v)=v-\langle v,\beta^\vee\rangle\beta$ preserves $P$ since both $v$ and $\beta$ lie there and the coefficient is integral; the root-coroot permutations, finiteness of the reflection group and reducedness are those of the datum on $X$, acting on the same rational vector space. By [lem-sfb-integral-root-datum-isogenies], realize this datum by a split reductive integral group $S$ with maximal torus $D_{\mathbf Z}(P)$. The roots still span $P\otimes\mathbf Q=V$, and the full weight lattice computed from these coroots is $P$ itself. The two fibre criteria of [lem-sfb-integral-split-root-datum] therefore make $S$ semisimple and simply connected on every geometric fibre, exactly in the sense required in the item.

The finite-index inclusion $u:X\hookrightarrow P$ satisfies the isogeny theorem with $G_0=Q$, $G_1=S$ and the identity bijection of roots: $u(\beta)=\beta$ and restriction of the coroot on $P$ is the coroot on $X$. Thus [lem-sfb-integral-root-datum-isogenies] supplies a finite faithfully flat finitely presented homomorphism $\pi:S\to Q$ with closed central kernel
$$F=D_{\mathbf Z}(P/X).$$
Since $P/X$ is finite, $\mathbf Z[P/X]$ is a free $\mathbf Z$-module on the finite basis $\{e_a:a\in P/X\}$. Thus $F$ is finite locally free, including at primes dividing its rank. In particular no prime-to-characteristic or reduced-kernel assumption has entered the construction.

source.place: Theorem 6.1.16(1), p.196; Definition 6.1.8 and Example 6.1.9, p.191; Appendix B.1, p.280.

proof.text: Let $\mathbf Z\to B$ be any ring map. The first quotient and its kernel remain the represented fppf quotient by the arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-relative-central-multiplicative-quotient]. The second map and its kernel remain faithfully flat, finitely presented and $D_B(P/X)$ by [lem-sfb-integral-root-datum-isogenies]. To verify its quotient interpretation explicitly, pull back the singleton fppf cover $S_B\to Q_B$ along any point $q:V\to Q_B$. By [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change] it gives a cover of $V$ on which $q$ lifts to $S_B$. Two lifts $s_1,s_2$ have the same image exactly when $s_1^{-1}s_2\in F_B$, by the kernel equality. Consequently the fppf sheafification of $S_B/F_B$ is $Q_B$. This proves the second exact sequence and its base-change assertion, with scheme-theoretic kernels throughout.

source.place: Definition 3.3.9, p.103; Appendix B.1; quotient torsor interpretation of Corollary 3.3.5, pp.100-101. Cover base change: Stacks Tag 021O, topologies.tex lemma-fppf (3).

proof.text: The chosen split tori remain products of $\mathbf G_m$ over $B$; $F_B$ has coordinate algebra $B[P/X]$, free on the same finite basis. Every geometric fibre over $B$ is obtained from an algebraically closed field equipped with a map from $\mathbf Z$, so the root-datum and fibre criteria already checked give the same semisimple and simply connected properties after this base change. These criteria are compatible with base change by [lem-sfb-integral-split-root-datum]. If $B$ is the zero ring the base scheme is empty and the assertions hold vacuously. For empty root data, $H$ is a torus, $T=H$ and $Q=S=1$; for a semisimple $H$, $C=0$ and $T=1$. Thus the allowed trivial cases introduce no exceptions.
